note: The second-closest ICP match in this batch after Soneel Raj, and like him he did not buy the coaching. He clears the commercial criteria: a long-tenured Amtrak engineering job, his own business consulting company, an active stock portfolio, and — decisively — he never raised affordability at all, confirming he would simply have put $4,000 on a credit card if he had wanted it. Neglected health is textbook and in the ICP's own words: a career and night shifts meant 'with the job and life, I haven't done anything consistently' for 10 to 15 years. The two misses are physical and they are real. He is roughly 30 pounds above his target weight with diagnosed type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol after a decade and a half of inactivity, which is rescue and reversal rather than good-to-great, and he is deconditioned by any reading — he sits all night on emergency standby and describes waking feeling like an old man. He is not the gym-averse profile the exclusion names, which is why this reads as edge rather than outside. The pattern across the batch is now hard to miss: the two prospects who best fit the stated ICP, Soneel Raj and Tony Moore, both declined the programme on value, while the prospects who bought sat outside it on income. The ICP is selecting for people who can afford the offer and do not want it.
